title: Sync root when updating the user password from the menu
head: 33f35319249b
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The ordinary wheel user cannot reach the root-status prompt or change their password
leads.consequence: The menu launches the helper as the desktop user. Arch shadow's passwd -S root refuses status requests for anyone whose real UID is neither root nor root's UID. With pipefail and set -e, root_status assignment aborts before either chpasswd branch. Even an already enabled root prevents the normal wheel account from changing its password through this menu; stderr from passwd is discarded and the terminal displays failure. The test stub wrongly grants every caller a root-status record. Perform the status lookup under appropriate privilege, distinguish a failed lookup from P, and add a non-root denial case to the fixture.

leads.summary: Cancelling the locked-root confirmation changes the user's password instead of cancelling
leads.consequence: For locked or unset root, the gum confirmation's nonzero result includes an explicit No and an interrupted/failed prompt. Both take the else branch and submit the user's new password alone through sudo chpasswd. If the user aborts at the confirmation, their password nevertheless changes and the command can exit zero. Handle cancellation separately from a deliberate No (or add a separate explicit user-only choice). Test interruption and confirm-command errors as well as a decline.

leads.summary: Open PR #9239 adds a different helper at precisely the new helper path
leads.consequence: Both this PR and #9239 add bin/omarchy-user-password and test/shell.d/user-password-test.sh, and both replace the same menu action. The other helper uses passwd plus a migration to wire pam_gnome_keyring into its password stack; this one uses chpasswd without that migration. A straightforward merge conflicts at the two added paths and menu row. Choosing just this helper would omit the other PR's password/keyring update path; choosing just the other would omit root synchronization. Reconcile both feature implementations and test fixtures if either lands first.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified with read-only gh (PR #9239 open, adds same two files, repoints update.password.user); Opus also verified in self-check; published as N5

leads.summary: The manual promises both accounts change in cases when only the login account changes
leads.consequence: The manual says the User and root row sets the login account and root to the same password without any qualification, but the new non-wheel path executes plain passwd and a declined locked-root prompt writes only the user record. The menu also labels the row 'User and root' for both cases. Document the conditional behavior; the mismatch becomes more visible if open child-install PR #9750 lands, because its newly provisioned child account is intentionally excluded from wheel and its parent/root password must stay separate.
leads.triage: label/manual mismatch already noted by Opus as minor leftover; published as N6. #9750 child-user premise unverified, dropped

prior_findings.reason: Original claim accurate. New check runs passwd -S root without sudo; shadow 4.20.0 passwd.c:1011-1025 refuses for non-root, so the flow exits 1 (N1) and never classifies root. Tolerating the error would restore F1 fully.

prior_findings.reason: Suggestion omitted that passwd -S root requires root; as written it cannot work for the menu caller. Corrected suggestion: sudo passwd -S root.

passwd -S root without sudo + set -euo pipefail: every wheel user gets exit 1 after two prompts, no password changed. Corroborated by Sol H1.
Ctrl+C (130) at gum confirm treated as No; user-only chpasswd proceeds. Reachable once N1 fixed. Corroborated by Sol H2.
NP = empty root password, usable under nullok; prompt text wrong and default keeps it. Rare.
Test stubs mis-model passwd -S and sudo; test passes on broken head and fails against correct fix.

Row label/manual say User and root but non-wheel and declined confirm change user only (Sol H4 and Opus minor leftover). #9750 part of H4 dropped as unverified.

# RETRO: #13215 follow-up

- Worked: the Sol hunt (4.6 min) independently found N1, N2, the #9239 conflict and the label mismatch; Opus found the same core issue with sandbox evidence and validated fixes.
- Lesson: the earlier public review's suggested command (`passwd -S root`) omitted the privilege it needs, and the author followed it literally. Suggested commands should be checked for the caller's privileges before publishing. The draft owns the correction.
- Opus self-check caught one real overstatement (`nullok` applies to console login, not `su`) and an exact-output formatting error; both fixed before the editorial check.
- Process deviation (Opus, self-reported): ran `go env GOMODCACHE` on the host (software probe outside review.py); the empty result made a grep recurse from `/` and it surfaced one path/line inside the private `sol/gum-src` directory (upstream gum source, not a Sol report). No conclusions exchanged; no finding depends on it. Independence is not materially affected since Sol is a hunter, not a peer reviewer. Suggest reviewer prompts warn against unguarded `$(...)/` path construction in host greps.
- Opus's final.md N3 wording "(for example su)" was self-corrected in draft-check; the draft does not carry it.
comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13215#issuecomment-5837943629) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13215#issuecomment-5841748520), checked at `33f35319`.

**Outcome:** four of the five earlier findings are resolved. The new locked-root check, however, stops the password change for every account in `wheel`, which includes the owner on every default install. That part traces back to the earlier review's own suggestion, corrected below.

| Earlier finding | Status at `33f35319` |
|---|---|
| Menu row always changes root, even when locked or unset | Not fixed: the new check fails, so the row now stops before changing anything (see below) |
| Non-wheel accounts lose the menu password option | Resolved |
| `manual/48-security.md` named the old _User_ row | Resolved |
| `user` group missing from CLI help | Resolved |
| Ctrl+C at a `gum input` prompt shows "Failed" | Resolved |

**Verified:** a non-wheel account now reaches plain `passwd` before any prompt, and `exec` passes its exit status through, including 130. The top-level `omarchy` listing now includes the `user` group with its description, and `omarchy user --help` shows the description. Both `gum input` prompts use `|| exit $?`, so Ctrl+C exits 130 and the launcher closes quietly. The manual names the _User and root_ row.

### The locked-root check makes the menu row fail for every wheel user

**Correction to the earlier review:** its suggested change said to check root with `passwd -S root` but did not say that this needs root. As a normal user it cannot work.

`bin/omarchy-user-password:24` runs `passwd -S root` as the logged-in user. The menu starts the script without elevation, and `omarchy:requires-sudo` is metadata only. shadow 4.20.0 refuses to show another account's status to a non-root caller (`src/passwd.c:1011-1025`, exit status 1). Under `set -euo pipefail` that failure ends the script:

```text
wheel user, current head
  gum input × 2               passwords entered and match
  passwd -S root              exit 1  (stderr sent to /dev/null)
  root_status=$(... | awk)    pipefail → assignment fails → errexit
  script                      exit 1 → window shows "Failed (exit code 1)"
  sudo chpasswd               never reached
```

The confirm prompt never appears, and neither password changes. The earlier head and the base both changed the password.

**Impact:** on a default install, the _User and root_ row asks for the new password twice and then fails with no explanation. If the error is simply tolerated instead (for example `|| true`), `root_status` is empty and root is always overwritten again, which is the original problem.

**Suggested change:** read the status through `sudo`, and let errors show:

```bash
root_status=$(sudo passwd -S root | awk '{print $2}')
```

The `sudo passwd -S root` line was tried in a sandbox with stubbed `sudo`, `passwd` and `chpasswd`. With it, a normal root syncs both accounts without a prompt, a locked root asks first, and a `sudo` failure exits 1 with nothing changed.

### Ctrl+C at the new root confirmation still changes the user's password

Once the check above works, a locked (`L`) or empty (`NP`) root shows `gum confirm`. gum 2.0.2 exits 130 on Ctrl+C, and the `else` branch at `:28-29` treats that as "No", so the script continues and sends the user-only line to `sudo chpasswd`.

**Impact:** cancelling at this prompt changes the login password instead of cancelling.

**Suggested change:** in the `else` branch, `status=$?; (( status == 130 )) && exit 130; sync_root=0`. In the same stubbed sandbox this exits 130 with no `chpasswd` call, while Esc and "No" still update the user only.

### Smaller notes

- **Empty root password (`NP`):** shadow reports `NP` for an empty hash. Arch's `system-auth` uses `pam_unix nullok`, so such a root can log in at a console with an empty password, the opposite of "no usable password". The prompt then defaults to leaving it that way. No Omarchy install path creates this state. Suggested change: confirm only for `L`, or reword the prompt for `NP`.
- **Optional test improvement:** the test's `passwd` stub answers `-S root` for any caller, and its `sudo` stub never runs the command. So the test passes on this head, fails as soon as the stub refuses `-S root` like shadow does, and also fails against the `sudo passwd -S root` fix above. Suggested change: have the `sudo` stub run `passwd`, make the `passwd` stub refuse `-S root` unless reached through `sudo`, and add Ctrl+C-at-confirm (expect 130, no `chpasswd`).
- **Label:** the row and the manual say _User and root_, but non-wheel accounts and a declined confirmation change only the user's password. A short mention in `manual/48-security.md` would cover it.
- **Related open PR:** #9239 also adds `bin/omarchy-user-password` and `test/shell.d/user-password-test.sh` and points the same menu row at it, with a different approach (plain `passwd` plus GNOME keyring sync). Whichever lands second needs to reconcile the two.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the new commit and the dependencies it relies on, at the versions Arch currently packages: shadow 4.20.0 (`passwd`, `chpasswd`), linux-pam 1.7.2, pambase and gum 2.0.2. The PR's test, variants of it, the suggested changes and scripted scenarios ran in an isolated sandbox with stubbed `gum`, `id`, `passwd`, `sudo` and `chpasswd`. The `passwd -S` refusal and the gum exit codes are modelled from source. No real `sudo`, `passwd`, `chpasswd`, PAM or account change was run, and the menu flow was not run on a desktop.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
